front.title: Delegation for Agentic AI in OAuth-Based Architectures: Requirements and Gap Analysis

abstract.t: The OAuth 2.0 authorization framework and its associated specifications define mechanisms for delegating authority from a resource owner to a client acting on its behalf. These mechanisms are designed mainly for a single-principal, single-hop model in which a human authorizes a client at authorization time (the client credentials grant, in which a client acts on its own behalf, is the exception). Agentic AI systems introduce a fundamentally different operational context: autonomous software agents that execute multi- hop delegation chains, propagate constrained authority across organizational boundaries, and perform consequential actions without continuous human involvement. This document analyzes the normative gaps between the requirements for secure delegation in Agentic AI systems and the coverage provided by the existing published OAuth 2.0 RFC corpus. Fifteen requirements decomposed into 111 sub- requirements are evaluated against 41 mechanisms, including 18 published RFCs, 11 Internet-Drafts, and 12 informative prior-art and non-IETF specifications. The analysis identifies 48 sub-requirements (43%) for which no published RFC provides normative coverage, and no sub-requirement that remains unaddressed by every evaluated mechanism; for 15 of these 48 gaps, no evaluated Internet-Draft is credited with complete coverage. This document does not define new protocol mechanisms. Its output defines the normative gaps that a companion solution specification must address to extend the OAuth 2.0 framework to support secure, accountable, and interoperable delegation in Agentic AI deployments.
